payload.headline: Tesla slips 1.18% to 380.14, stuck under resistance; still avoid

summary.thesis: Tesla's sales have stalled, and its margins and cash flow are shrinking, yet the stock trades near the top of its own valuation history at 418.3 times earnings.
summary.decision: Long-term: avoid. Swing: wait, because the price sits just under a resistance zone that has turned it back 9 times and there is no trend.
summary.act_at: Re-examine near 293.94 only if margin recovers; no swing trade until a close above 404.4

payload.happening: Tesla closed at 380.14, down 1.18% on the day. That is just below a resistance zone at 380.15–389.95, a price band where rallies have stalled 9 times. The 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (382.15, 377.17, 381.15) are all flat, and the trend is marked as a range. There is no new news since yesterday's note, which covered a reported SpaceX merger. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
payload.business: The latest filing (2026-10-22) points to a business that has slowed. Revenue in the latest quarter was -0.17% versus a year earlier, down from 15.78% growth two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Trailing free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) halved, from 6.8B to 3.3B. Inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%. Unsold cars can force price cuts that squeeze margins further. Returns on new investment have dropped to 5¢ per dollar a year from 33¢ three years ago, so heavy spending is not paying back yet. What is not at risk is the balance sheet: net cash is 37.5B and total liquidity is 45.4B, against 8.0B of debt. Share dilution is small at 0.43%. The reported SpaceX merger changes governance and sentiment, not demand or margins, unless terms are filed.

worth.text: At 380.14, Tesla is valued at about 1503.0B. That is 14.5 times sales and 418.3 times trailing earnings per share of 0.91. A cash-flow model (DCF: today's value of future cash) built on trailing free cash flow of 3.3B and a 9.9% discount rate gives 20.17 / 24.93 / 45.0 per share for bear / base / bull. Even assuming 30% starting growth, it reaches only 45.31. The filings risk note says the price needs about 51% a year growth, while the company has delivered 3% a year over 3 years. Against its own history, the price-to-sales ratio is at the 75th percentile of the past 5 years. That method maps to 203.8 / 293.94 / 399.81, so the stock sits close to the top of that range. The gap between the two methods comes down to one thing. The DCF prices today's small cash flow, while the history method assumes the market keeps paying the rich sales multiples it has paid before. With sales flat and margins falling, a fair range is the low-to-middle part of Tesla's own history.
worth.key_assumption: With flat quarterly sales and operating margin down to 3.35%, the market values Tesla in the low-to-middle part of its 5-year price-to-sales range rather than near the 399.81 top.

bull: Net cash of 37.5B and liquidity of 45.4B give Tesla room to keep investing through a slow patch.
Revenue over the last 12 months still grew 8.3%, to 103.6B from 95.6B.
Analysts' next-year EPS growth assumption is 25%; if delivered, the DCF value rises toward the 34.01–45.31 range shown for 20–30% starting growth.
bear: The price needs about 51% a year growth, versus 3% a year delivered over 3 years.
Trailing free cash flow fell to 3.3B from 6.8B, and operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%.
Inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%, which can force price cuts that hurt margins further.

levels.what: Today's close. It sits near the own-history top of 399.81 and far above the DCF base of 24.93, so value gives the price no support here.
Bottom of the nearest support zone (363.86–368.76), where buyers have stepped in 4 times. A close below it points to the next zone at 349.24–354.14.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range. Re-examine here only if the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74%.

longterm.why: Sales growth, margins, cash flow and returns on investment are all weakening, while the price sits near the top of its own valuation history. The internal committee call is Reduce, and the business grade is D.

swing.why: The price sits just under resistance at 380.15–389.95 (9 touches), the averages are flat and the trend is a range, so there is no clean setup. No trade until a close above 404.4, or until a pullback holds at 363.86–368.76.

decision.timing: No new long-term position before the 2027-01-27 report. Options price an 11.2% move by 2026-12-18 and a 19.6% move by 2027-02-19, which covers the report. Recent actual swings (72.9) have been bigger than what options imply (53.6), and any filed merger terms could move the price before earnings.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly revenue growth back above 0% versus a year earlier.
Trailing free cash flow climbs back toward 6.8B while inventory growth falls back to the pace of sales growth.
The price falls toward the 293.94 own-history midpoint with margins stable, which would make a long-term look worthwhile; a close below 363.86 would instead strengthen the avoid.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid; the 1.18% drop to 380.14 left the price below the 380.15–389.95 resistance zone and still near the top of its own valuation range, while the trend label moved from down to range.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
